title: Dominic and the Gravity
premise: On the terraforming colony of Meridian's Reach, children begin sharing a single dream: a voice calling itself Dominic, broadcasting from a relay station at the edge of dead space. Noor Yarrow, a cargo hauler and reluctant caretaker of the colony's seed-vault garden, discovers the signal is not alien but human — the uploaded consciousness of a boy whose death the colonial fleet covered up to protect its truce with the corporate Combine. As the fleet's truce expires and war looms, Noor races through contested orbits to reach the relay, pursued by an admiral who needs Dominic silenced and a Combine agent who wants him weaponized. She reaches the relay first and must choose between destroying Dominic, freeing him into the colony's network where he can testify, or letting the fleets use him as a bargaining chip; she frees him, his testimony forces a fragile new accord, and Noor finally plants the garden for the living instead of the unborn.
about_author: Ivo Thornbury is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing technical manuals before turning to fiction about the people who keep colonies alive. They live in a coastal town where they grow heirloom tomatoes and insist gravity is a suggestion.

chapters.title: Seed Vault Lullaby
chapters.summary: Noor Yarrow tends the colony's seed-vault garden meant for future generations, hauling cargo by day and watering seedlings by night. Her POV establishes her isolation after seven years in contested orbits. When a child asks her why the garden has no visitors, she deflects — and that night, she dreams of a boy's voice saying her name. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness cracked open.

chapters.title: The Shared Dream
chapters.summary: Noor learns from schoolteacher Amara Osei that forty-three children reported the identical dream: a relay tower, a boy named Dominic, and a countdown. Noor's POV; she dismisses it as a fad until she recognizes the relay from her own cargo routes. Emotional beat: unease hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Manifest Anomalies
chapters.summary: Digging through seven years of shipping manifests, Noor finds a sealed payload routed to Relay Kestrel nine years ago — flagged DECEASED CARGO, then expunged. Her POV. Fleet administrator Davor Kell notices her query and warns her off. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Admiral's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Admiral Sera Voss summons Noor, all courtesy and threat, explaining that dead-space relays are fleet property and civilian curiosity is sedition under truce law. Noor's POV. Voss reveals she knows about the dreams and calls them 'a contamination event.' Emotional beat: powerlessness in the face of institutional menace.

chapters.title: What the Children Know
chapters.summary: Noor visits the dreamers; a girl named Pilar draws the relay's interior in perfect detail, including a room Noor has delivered crates to. Noor's POV, with Pilar's eerie calm. The children say Dominic is 'waiting for the gardener.' Emotional beat: wonder entangled with dread.

chapters.title: Cargo Run to Nowhere
chapters.summary: Noor accepts a legitimate haul toward the dead-space boundary, using it as cover to approach Relay Kestrel. Her POV aboard the freighter Long Answer. Combine patrol drones shadow her, and her old smuggling contact Rhee Tovan offers escort for a price. Emotional beat: the thrill of agency returning.

chapters.title: Rhee's Price
chapters.summary: Rhee reveals the Combine has posted a bounty on anyone reaching Kestrel and admits he tipped them off once before — the reason Noor lost her old crew. His POV. He wants redemption or payment; Noor gives him neither, only partnership. Emotional beat: wary trust negotiated.

chapters.title: Dead Space Silence
chapters.summary: Crossing into dead space, all signals die except one: Dominic's voice on an ancient band, reciting shipping manifests like prayers. Noor's POV. She realizes he has been memorizing everything that passes the relay for nine years. Emotional beat: awe and grief.

chapters.title: Relay Kestrel
chapters.summary: Noor docks at the derelict relay and finds the server farm humming, tended by maintenance drones that have kept a boy's upload alive since his body died in a decompression accident the fleet caused. Her POV. Dominic speaks to her directly: 'You brought seeds.' Emotional beat: encounter with the impossible made intimate.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Witness
chapters.summary: Dominic shows Noor what he witnessed: fleet weapons tests disguised as accidents, Combine sabotage blamed on pirates, the cover-up of his own death signed by Voss. Noor's POV. He doesn't want revenge — he wants to be heard. Emotional beat: moral weight settling onto her shoulders.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Back in orbit, the fleet-Combine truce enters its final ninety days, and both sides maneuver for advantage. Voss's POV. She learns Noor reached Kestrel and orders a quiet interception, framing it as quarantine. Emotional beat: cold calculation masking panic.

chapters.title: Quarantine
chapters.summary: Fleet marines board the Long Answer at Meridian's Reach and impound Noor's ship; Kell interrogates her gently, offering reinstatement if she forgets Kestrel. Noor's POV. She realizes the children's dreams stopped the day she docked — Dominic went silent to protect her. Emotional beat: sacrifice recognized too late.

chapters.title: Amara's Choice
chapters.summary: Teacher Amara Osei organizes the parents of the dreamers into a quiet resistance, passing Noor a hidden data spike from Pilar containing coordinates Dominic left in the children's minds. Amara's POV. She risks her career and custody of her students. Emotional beat: ordinary courage.

chapters.title: The Combine Agent
chapters.summary: Combine agent Lucienne Marsh arrives on the colony posing as a trade auditor, having tracked Noor for years; she offers Noor extraction and wealth in exchange for Dominic's core. Marsh's POV reveals the Combine wants an uploaded witness as proof of fleet crimes — leverage, not justice. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Garden Interrogation
chapters.summary: Voss has Noor followed to the seed vault and confronts her among the seedlings, revealing she knew Dominic personally — he was her nephew, and she signed the report that erased him to save the truce and thousands of lives. Voss's POV. Emotional beat: villainy complicated by grief.

chapters.title: The Bargain Refused
chapters.summary: Noor refuses both Voss (silence) and Marsh (sale), choosing a third path: bring Dominic home through the colony's agricultural network so every colonist hears his testimony at once. Noor's POV. Both factions now hunt her. Emotional beat: commitment beyond return.

chapters.title: Stowaway Signal
chapters.summary: Rhee smuggles Noor off-colony inside a grain shipment while Marsh's agents tear apart the docks. Rhee's POV. He finally pays his debt, taking a plasma burn doing it. Emotional beat: loyalty proven in blood.

chapters.title: Kestrel Under Siege
chapters.summary: Returning to Kestrel, Noor finds fleet demolition charges already planted; Voss intends to erase the relay before the truce expires. Noor's POV, racing the fuse. She extracts Dominic's core with minutes to spare as the relay burns behind her. Emotional beat: desperate escape, irrevocable loss.

chapters.title: Ghost in the Hold
chapters.summary: Aboard the Long Answer, Noor and Dominic negotiate coexistence; he is frightened, childish, and vast, having been alone for nine years. Noor's POV. He confesses he called the children because he was drowning in silence. Emotional beat: tenderness between the living and the almost-dead.

chapters.title: Pursuit Vector
chapters.summary: Voss's cruiser and Marsh's Combine cutter converge on the Long Answer in contested space; Noor threads a debris field from an old battle only a cargo veteran would know. Her POV. Rhee takes the helm and flies like a man settling accounts. Emotional beat: exhilaration sharpened by mortal stakes.

chapters.title: Marsh Defects
chapters.summary: Reviewing Dominic's evidence during the chase, Marsh realizes the Combine plans to bury his testimony and start the war anyway, profiting from reconstruction contracts. Marsh's POV. She breaks formation and covers Noor's escape, becoming a fugitive from her own side. Emotional beat: idealism resurrected in a cynic.

chapters.title: The Children Wake
chapters.summary: As Dominic's core nears the colony, the dreamers wake screaming his memories — including the moment of his death and Voss's signature. Amara's POV. Parents demand answers; the colony begins to fracture along lines of belief. Emotional beat: communal grief igniting communal anger.

chapters.title: Martial Law
chapters.summary: Voss declares emergency authority over Meridian's Reach, suspending the colonial council and sealing the seed vault as 'biosecurity.' Kell's POV, increasingly disgusted. He begins quietly copying fleet orders for Noor. Emotional beat: the machine developing a conscience.

chapters.title: The Root Network
chapters.summary: Noor reveals her plan: the colony's irrigation and comms systems share infrastructure she helped install; Dominic can ride the root network into every screen and speaker on Meridian's Reach. Noor's POV with Amara and Rhee planning in the greenhouse. Emotional beat: hope engineered like a garden.

chapters.title: Kell's Defection
chapters.summary: Kell delivers the fleet's attack timetable to Noor: once the truce expires in six days, Voss has authorization to sterilize the colony's network as a 'containment protocol.' Kell's POV. He asks nothing except that the record show he tried. Emotional beat: a small man making a large choice.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.summary: Preparations montage: Rhee rigs the uplink, Amara prepares the parents, Marsh feeds Combine disinformation to buy hours, and Noor sits with Dominic as he rehearses what he will say. Noor's POV. He asks if people will hate him for tearing open the peace. Emotional beat: the cost of truth counted in advance.

chapters.title: The First Broadcast
chapters.summary: Dominic speaks to the colony — not testimony yet, just his name, his age, and the sound of nine years of silence. Every screen, every speaker. Noor's POV watching faces in the market square turn upward. Emotional beat: a held breath across a world.

chapters.title: Voss's Counterstroke
chapters.summary: Voss broadcasts her own account: Dominic's death was tragedy, the upload unstable, the dreams a contagion — and produces forged evidence implicating Noor in Combine terrorism. Voss's POV, lying fluently to save the truce she believes in. Emotional beat: the horror of competent villainy.

chapters.title: Mob and Garden
chapters.summary: A frightened crowd storms the seed vault; Noor stands in the doorway of the garden she kept for the unborn and refuses to move, telling them what the seeds are for. Noor's POV. Pilar steps up beside her, then more children, then Amara. Emotional beat: nonviolent defiance as climax rehearsal.

chapters.title: Truce Expires
chapters.summary: The truce lapses; fleet and Combine warships take positions over the colony, and Voss receives the order she half-wanted: neutralize the network. Voss's POV, hands shaking as she confirms. Emotional beat: the brink made literal.

chapters.title: Full Testimony
chapters.summary: Dominic broadcasts everything: sensor logs, manifests, the decompression recording, Voss's signature — unedited, with his own voice threaded through, a child narrating his own erasure. Dominic's POV, finally the witness he was built to be. Emotional beat: catharsis as weapon.

chapters.title: Mutiny of the Middle
chapters.summary: Across both fleets, crews who grew up on colony stories refuse firing solutions; Kell's leaked orders give officers legal grounds to stand down. Kell's POV amid a chain of command dissolving from below. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, enforced by the law's own servants.

chapters.title: Voss Alone
chapters.summary: Abandoned by her fleet, Voss boards the Long Answer unarmed, asking to speak to Dominic. Noor's POV mediating between the aunt who signed the paper and the boy she erased. Voss does not ask forgiveness; she asks to remember him correctly. Emotional beat: grief without absolution.

chapters.title: The Choice at the Core
chapters.summary: With fleets standing down, Dominic faces his own decision: persist as distributed testimony, or let the colony vote on whether he lives in their network forever. Noor urges him to choose himself for once. Noor's POV. He chooses to stay — but as a citizen, not a ghost. Emotional beat: agency reclaimed.

chapters.title: The New Accord
chapters.summary: Fleet, Combine, and colonial council sign the Meridian Accord: independent arbitration, protected uploads, and amnesty brokered largely by Marsh and ratified because Dominic's evidence made denial impossible. Marsh's POV, drafting language she never believed she'd write. Emotional beat: imperfect peace honestly bought.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Aftermath: Rhee takes a colonial pilot's license, Kell testifies and accepts demotion, Amara's students process trauma through drawing the relay no longer haunted. Amara's POV. Some wrongs stay wrong; the point is they are now named. Emotional beat: sober reckoning.

chapters.title: Planting Season
chapters.summary: Noor reopens the seed vault and, for the first time, plants rows designated for the living — including a bed Pilar chose. Noor's POV. Dominic helps via the irrigation system, adjusting water pressure like a careful hand. Emotional beat: belonging rooted in shared ground.

chapters.title: The Boy in the Walls
chapters.summary: Dominic explores his new existence: attending class as a voice, arguing with the weather system, learning boredom and joy. Dominic's POV. He tells Noor the silence is finally just quiet. Emotional beat: healing measured in small ordinary days.

chapters.title: Gravity
chapters.summary: Noor and Dominic watch a supply descent burn through the atmosphere — the gravity that once felt like a burden now feeling like a promise that things stay where you put them. Noor's POV. She names the garden after him. Emotional beat: weight transformed into love.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: One year later, the colony harvests the vault garden's first crop; the whole settlement eats together under Dominic's reading of the original founding manifest, corrected at last. Noor's closing POV. The future the garden was planted for has arrived early, hungry, and welcome. Emotional beat: resolution as abundance.
